sources.title: Interview note preserving the hand-written topological-sort request

claims.text: The recoverable source only asks the candidate to hand-write topological sort; it does not prescribe Java, graph representation, ordering policy, algorithm variant, or cycle API.
Java vertices 0..V-1, int[][] directed edges, any valid topological order, Kahn processing, and exception-on-cycle are explicit answer-side choices.
The Java implementation matches an independent permutation-existence oracle over every simple directed graph through four vertices and passes larger seeded DAG plus boundary validation.

validation.command: extract candidate Java; javac -Xlint:all -Werror; independent permutation-existence oracle for all simple directed graphs through V=4 plus seeded DAG validation
validation.reported_stdout: PASS exhaustive_graphs=4166 exhaustive_dags=573 exhaustive_cycles=3593 randomized_dags=800 oracle=permutation-validity duplicates=pass invalid=reject
checks: all 4166 simple directed graphs through four vertices classified by independent permutation oracle
all 573 exhaustive DAGs return a valid vertex permutation respecting every edge
800 seeded DAGs up to 40 vertices return valid orders
duplicate edges remain balanced by indegree/decrement accounting
empty graph and declared invalid-input boundaries pass

boundary_tests.expected: review validates edge precedence and vertex uniqueness rather than one fixed array
self-cycle and multi-vertex cycles reject under declared API

findings: The repository source preserves only a hand-written topological-sort request; Java, graph representation, vertex numbering, Kahn/BFS, ordering policy and cycle API are not recovered source constraints.
The candidate explicitly labels Java, 0..V-1 vertices, int[][] directed edges, arbitrary-valid-order semantics, Kahn processing and exception-on-cycle as answer-side choices.

The Kahn invariant and cycle argument are sound for the declared contract: only current zero-indegree vertices are emitted, outgoing edges are removed once per edge record, and an empty frontier with unprocessed vertices implies a directed cycle.

An independent permutation-existence oracle, using neither Kahn nor DFS cycle detection, validates every simple directed graph through four vertices: 4,166 graphs total, 573 DAGs accepted with valid orders and 3,593 cyclic graphs rejected.
Reviewer checks additionally validate 800 seeded DAGs up to 40 vertices, duplicate-edge bookkeeping, self/cyclic rejection, empty graph behavior and declared invalid-input boundaries.
No fixed-order assumption, fabricated project experience, unsupported source expansion or unresolved source variant was found.
